title: Question 14710
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Question ID: 14710_bethany_books_safe

Timothy worked the register at Bethany Books & Brew, a privately owned Christian bookstore café. One night after the café closed, Timothy discovered that the amount of cash in the register did not match the register’s receipt roll. He put the cash and the receipt roll into a bank bag, gave the bag to Lydia, the store manager, and reported the discrepancy.

Lydia immediately accused Timothy of taking money from the register and threatened to fire him if he did not make up the difference. Lydia placed the bag in the office safe. Angry at what he considered an unjust accusation, Timothy waited until Lydia left the room and then reached into the still-open safe, took the bag containing the cash, and left with it.

Timothy is guilty of
rightExplanation:
A is correct. Timothy took the bag from the safe after Lydia had received it and placed it there. The answer array is built around the larceny/embezzlement possession line.

Gold Key: Larceny is the trespassory taking/carrying away of another’s property with intent to permanently deprive. Embezzlement requires conversion by someone who already had lawful possession when the conversion occurred.

Silver Key: In a larceny/embezzlement answer array, do not stop at “employee handled money.” Find who had control at the moment the defendant took the property for himself. Here, after Timothy handed the bag to Lydia and Lydia put it in the safe, the later taking is larceny territory.

wrongExplanations.B: Embezzlement is the trap. Timothy earlier handled the cash as cashier, but the decisive event is later: he gave the bag to Lydia, Lydia put it in the safe, and Timothy then reached into the safe and took it. Gold Key: embezzlement needs lawful possession at the time of conversion. The safe fact moves the question away from embezzlement.
wrongExplanations.C: “Both” overcounts. The facts support larceny, but the possession-reset fact blocks embezzlement. A student picks C by noticing two time periods: Timothy had the money at the register, then later took it from the safe. Silver Key: collapse the array to the moment of wrongful taking. One moment controls; do not stack two crimes from two time slices.
wrongExplanations.D: “Neither” ignores the final taking. Even if Timothy felt falsely accused, he reached into the safe, took the cash bag, and left with it. That answers the larceny side of the array.

c3.label: C: both larceny and embezzlement
c3.text: Cut as overcount / half-truth. It captures the larceny side but adds embezzlement without the needed possession frame.

c3.label: D: neither larceny nor embezzlement
c3.text: Cut because the final safe-taking keeps at least larceny alive.

c3.label: A vs. B
c3.text:
larceny only vs. embezzlement only.
* Axis: who had possession/control at the moment Timothy took the bag for himself?
* Splitting fact: Timothy had already handed the bag to Lydia, and Lydia placed it in the safe.
* Result: larceny, not embezzlement.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: No residual tie after the Gold Key. Answer A remains.

studentScript: This is a larceny/embezzlement matrix. Freeze the taking moment. Timothy gave the bag to Lydia; Lydia put it in the safe; Timothy later took it from the safe. That is larceny only. Pick A.

A.signal: Matches the safe-taking fact once the possession Gold Key is applied.
A.lawyer: Correct because Timothy took property from the store/manager's control after he had turned it over.

B.signal: Looks at Timothy's employee/register role instead of the later safe-taking moment.
B.lawyer: Embezzlement requires lawful possession at conversion; Timothy did not have that after handing the bag to Lydia.

C.signal: Captures larceny but stacks embezzlement onto the same taking.
C.lawyer: The facts support larceny but not embezzlement.

D.signal: Ignores the later taking from the safe.
D.lawyer: The later taking and carrying away supports larceny.

goldKeys.statement: Larceny is the wrongful taking from another's possession; embezzlement is conversion by someone who already had lawful possession. In cashier/safe facts, ask who controlled the property when the defendant decided to take it for himself.
goldKeys.trigger: employee first handles business cash, then hands it to manager, then later takes it back
goldKeys.unlocks: larceny vs embezzlement when an employee handled property earlier but later takes it from the manager/safe
goldKeys.authority: Moore v. United States, 160 U.S. 268 (1895); common-law larceny definition

silverKeys.statement: For larceny/embezzlement arrays, freeze the timeline at the moment the defendant takes the property for himself; earlier lawful handling is not automatically the controlling moment.
silverKeys.trigger: answer choices list larceny, embezzlement, both, neither

remediation.title: Do not stop at employee-handled-money
remediation.signal: Employee touches business cash, then manager/store regains control, then employee takes it back.
remediation.studentMove: Ask who had control at the later wrongful taking.
remediation.tinyRule: Possession at conversion controls embezzlement; wrongful taking from another's possession points to larceny.
